text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes include increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue as high blood sugar affects how your body uses energy.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work harder to remove excess glucose, which pulls water from your tissues and makes you pee more often.
Extreme fatigue: Your cells cannot absorb glucose properly for energy without effective insulin, leaving you feeling constantly exhausted.
Blurred vision: Fluid shifts caused by high blood sugar can swell the lenses in your eyes, making it hard to focus.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: High blood sugar impairs your immune response and blood circulation, making minor wounds take much longer to heal.
Numbness or tingling: Peripheral nerve damage from elevated blood sugar can cause a prickly or numb sensation in your hands and feet.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety dark patches in body creases like the neck or armpits—known as acanthosis nigricans—often signal insulin resistance.
Frequent infections: Yeast infections or urinary tract infections happen more easily because bacteria and yeast thrive on excess glucose.
